label: L-03
title: Routes and ethPool are validated against sya.rewardToken() only at set time; an SYA setRewardToken bricks harvest and the harvester owner cannot pre-stage the new config
description: Cached cross-contract configuration validated against a live dependency only at write time; harvest reads the dependency live.
impact: None. Fail-loud harvest outage between SYA's setRewardToken and the harvester owner re-registering routes/ethPool.
attackPath: SYA owner switches rewardToken; every harvest reverts (fork: WrappedError 0x90bfb865); the harvester owner cannot pre-stage the new config (rejected before the switch, old config rejected after).
likelihood: low - requires a rare cross-owner migration
severityRationale: Cross-owner footgun (a competent owner would expect to pre-stage), but the impact it unlocks is only a temporary, loud availability gap on a helper contract, with no value at risk and recovery by an ordinary owner call. Low with runbook guidance. Distinct root from SYA M-02 (sya14m02, fixed).
recommendation: Check `Currency.unwrap(ethPool.currency1) == sya.rewardToken()` at the top of harvest with a named error; document 'clear/re-register harvester routes + ethPool' in the SYA reward-token migration runbook.
safeConfigGuidance: Put 'clear and re-register harvester routes + ethPool immediately after setRewardToken' in the SYA reward-token migration runbook.
evidence: CodeScan01RewardTokenForkTest: 'SYA rewardToken -> USDT', 'harvest ok false' (revert 0x90bfb865 WrappedError from the V4 currency transfer path), 'old ethPool rejected 0xc70c704d' (InvalidEthPool).

crossReferences.faithfulness_noNewFinding: story-001 Implementation Notes accepted the set-time check as harmless; CODE-004 shows the accepted risk is wider (cannot pre-stage).

crossProjectReferences.label: M-02
crossProjectReferences.note: SYA M-02 was SYA's own setRewardToken re-keying the nudge stream and bricking SYA.claim(); fixed at 6eab35c. DEDUP-004 is the harvester's own cached routes/ethPool validated against sya.rewardToken() only at set time, which an SYA reward-token switch makes stale and cannot be pre-staged. The cause is in harvester code, so it is not suppressed. Related: SYA L-10 (sya14l10, open), a standing phlimbo allowance kept across a setRewardToken repoint. The same cross-owner rotation hazard, but a different root.
